title: Proof-of-Value: Reserved GPUs + Burst Strategy — Kythera Analytics
next_steps: Redwood to share POC pricing table and reserved GPU tier options
SE to provide benchmark checklist and sample load script
Customer to provision test dataset and expected traffic traces by 2026-04-01
Schedule 1-hour benchmark run with Kythera on 2026-04-08
action_items: Ava Thompson: Send reserved + burst pricing and contract template (due 2026-04-02)
Ravi Patel: Create tailored benchmark config (models, sequence lengths, qps profile) and load script (due 2026-04-03)
Maya Chen: Share 7 days of traffic traces and 50 representative prompts (due 2026-04-01)
Owen Brooks: Grant Redwood test VPC access or provide VPN details for private POC (due 2026-04-05)
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-30 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m | Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Maya (Kythera Head of ML), Owen (Kythera Infra), Sana (Kythera CTO)
summary: POC scoping to determine reserved GPU sizing, burst capacity plan and fallback policies. Discussed success criteria (latency P95 targets, throughput, cost), benchmarking approach, timeline for running load tests, and security/VPC needs. Agreed next steps and owner assignment.
transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're on for about an hour. quick intros?
[00:12] Maya: Maya here, head of ml at Kythera. We run inference for our analytics summarizations and customer facing insights.
[00:22] Owen: Owen, infra. I own the k8s clusters and networking.
[00:27] Sana: Sana, CTO, quick hello.
[00:30] Ravi: Ravi with Redwood SE, I'll lead the benchmark and sizing side.
[00:34] Ava: Great. Objective today is to agree success criteria and scoping details for a proof of value — reserved GPUs with a burst strategy and clear fallback policies.
[00:48] Maya: High level: our workload is a mix. 70% short summary requests (avg 120 tokens) and 30% longer analysis reports (avg 1,200 tokens). Patterns are spiky — daytime hourly peaks, occasional batch overnight. We care about P95 latency for the interactive path, ideally sub 350ms for short summaries.
[01:12] Owen: To add, our peak qps for summaries hits about 220 qps for a 10 minute window during morning bursts. Sustained midday is more like 45 qps. Concurrency per request varies, but token lengths drive GPU utilization.
[01:30] Ravi: Okay good. For POC we'll need to model both tails. Typical approach: reserved capacity sized for steady baseline — maybe 8x A100-equivalent GPUs? But that's a guess, we need to map to model choice and quantization.
[01:50] Ava: Let's not lock hardware yet. For pricing and contract we will show two tiers: reserved baseline (committed), plus burst credits for transient peaks. The burst can be warm GPUs in the same region or fallback to slightly smaller model variants.
[02:08] Owen: Warm GPUs meaning pre-provisioned but charged only when used? or is there a warm pool style we can autoscale into?
[02:18] Ravi: Redwood Dedicated supports a burst pool — reserved nodes maintain baseline throughput and we have autoscaling rules that can spawn burst nodes. Warm pool means faster ramp but usually some cost for keeping VMs ready. We can configure cooldown windows, per-minute ramp, and a hard-cap fallback policy.
[02:36] Maya: For us it's important that when burst capacity is exhausted we have deterministic behavior: either degrade to a smaller model with known quality delta, or queue requests with a retry/backoff that keeps 95% of UX within SLO. We cannot silently spike latency to multiple seconds.
[02:54] Sana: Also audit and data residency — we need KMS integration and logs for each request for compliance.
[03:02] Ava: We will include audit logs and KMS in the private POC plan. For the hosted POC we can also provide VPC peering or private link.
[03:10] Ravi: For sizing I'll propose a benchmark matrix: short path model A (e.g., Llama2-70B-8k quantized to int8), short path model B (a distilled 13B), and a large model for long reports. We'll vary sequence lengths: 120, 512, 1200 tokens and run steady-state and spike profiles to capture cold vs warm KV cache effects.
[03:36] Maya: Can you include KV cache hit rate impact? our prompts reuse similar prefixes often.
[03:41] Ravi: Yes, KV cache is key — we'll run runs with prefix caching enabled. That can reduce tokens/time for long sessions.
[03:48] Owen: On networking — we prefer POC in us-east-1. We'll provide a read-only dataset and synthetic traffic trace. Are there tooling constraints for generating the load?
[03:58] Ravi: We'll supply a dockerized load generator and a JMeter-style script, but we prefer k6/vegeta. It will simulate qps, burst ramp and token lengths.
[04:08] Maya: Success criteria: 1) P95 latency for short summaries <= 350ms; 2) end-to-end 99th percentile for long reports <= 4s; 3) less than 1% error rate under target load; 4) cost per 1k responses below our internal threshold.
[04:30] Ava: Good, we'll encode those into the POC acceptance checklist.
[04:34] Sana: Timeline question — how quickly can Redwood get reserved GPUs allocated and do an initial benchmark?
[04:40] Ravi: If we have network access and the dataset by 2026-04-05, we can run a smoke benchmark within 48 hours and a full run by 2026-04-08. Reserved capacity provisioning for Dedicated might take a few days depending on availability; we can use hosted burst in the meantime.
[04:58] Owen: Any fallback policy patterns you recommend? e.g., when autoscale fails or burst exhausted.
[05:04] Ravi: Common patterns: 1) Model tiering — serve short summaries from a distilled 13B when burst exhausted; 2) Degraded feature mode — reduce output length or remove optional enhancements; 3) Queue with progressive backoff and client-side retry guidance; 4) Geographical fallback to another region if latency still fine. We should choose deterministic rules for each threshold.
[05:27] Maya: We prefer model tiering + short backoff; but show us the expected quality delta for tiering. We can't surprise customers with worse answers.
[05:37] Ravi: We'll run side-by-side A/B evals during the benchmark with a small prompts set to quantify the delta. We'll produce BLEU-like or embedding cosine deltas and human spot-checks.
[05:49] Ava: Pricing note — burst credits are metered. We'll provide examples of cost under a peak day and under steady state so finance can sign off.
[05:58] Owen: On monitoring, we need token-level cost, per-route latency, and tracing for request IDs to tie logs to audit events.
[06:06] Ravi: Redwood Console exposes per-route dashboards, token cost, and you can export traces to your tracing stack. We'll include a brief dashboard demo during the benchmark review.
[06:18] Maya: Ok what about model pinning and rollouts? We want to test model variants but have a safe rollback.
[06:25] Ava: Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback. We can pin by customer route or key.
[06:31] Owen: Security — we need to ensure keys use our KMS in the POC and that logs can be ingested into our SIEM.
[06:39] Ravi: We can integrate with your KMS and push logs to your ELK or Splunk. We'll add an audit log export step to the POC.
[06:48] Maya: For benchmarks, can you show us memory footprint and GPU utilization metrics? Some models have weird mem spikes.
[06:55] Ravi: Yes we'll collect top-level host metrics: GPU util, memory, swap, process OOMs, and per-request latency histograms. We'll also record tokenizer throughput.
[07:08] Ava: Quick note — if the team wants an on-prem/private deployment, that adds time for security review and potentially on-prem packaging. That would be a separate track in parallel.
[07:19] Sana: We might consider private if compliance requires it, but we'd like to see hosted/Dedicated first.
[07:24] Owen: Cost modelling — we need per-token cost and per-1k-response cost for each model variant.
[07:31] Ravi: We'll produce the cost analysis from the benchmark results showing tokens, latency, and dollars per 1k.
[07:37] Maya: Can the POC include a small integration test with our web front end? We want to validate end-to-end UX.
[07:44] Ava: Yes, we can run an integration test using your staging key and route. We'll coordinate with Owen for network access.
[07:50] Owen: We'll create a staging route and a short-lived key.
[07:53] Ravi: On autoscaling policies: we recommend a layered policy — scale up based on GPU queue length and token backlog, and scale down with a longer cooldown to avoid oscillation. For burst, set a ceiling and alerting.
[08:08] Maya: And circuit-breaker thresholds? we need to fail open or closed?
[08:12] Ravi: We typically fail-safe to a smaller model (fail open meaning degrade gracefully). But for sensitive calls you can fail closed. We'll configure per-route.
[08:22] Ava: Let's capture the acceptance criteria again and owners.
[08:26] Maya: P95 <= 350ms short, P99 <= 4s long, less than 1% errors, documented similarity delta for tiering < 0.1 embedding cosine drop on average.
[08:40] Ravi: Noted. For the benchmark we will prepare: model matrix, token lengths, qps profile (steady + 10m spike at 220 qps), KV cache scenarios, and the evaluation prompts.
[08:55] Owen: We'll provide network access details and sample traces.
[08:59] Sana: One last compliance note — will Redwood provide SOC 2 docs and ISO attestation?
[09:05] Ava: Yes we'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and the security package after the call.
[09:10] Maya: Great.
[09:12] [CRITICAL SHIFT TO ACTIONS] Ava: I'll send the POC checklist, pricing, and schedule. Ravi will send the benchmark config. Maya and Owen will share traces and networking.
[09:25] Owen: timeline recap — dataset by 4/1, benchmark config ready by 4/3, smoke run 4/6, full run 4/8.
[09:34] Ravi: That aligns. We'll also prepare the tiering evaluation and produce a documented fallback policy.
[09:42] Maya: Thanks everyone. We expect an internal readout week of 4/13.
[09:48] Ava: Perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and a short demo of the console.
[09:55] [END] Note: transcription has occasional misheard words (e.g., "cache" transcribed as "cash", proper nouns sometimes off).
